notes: This reading used only the assigned page, its C/H texts, supplied packet/current notation and the fixed instructions/conventions. The original image and each supplied overlapping full-resolution half were personally inspected once, line by line against both witnesses, including agreements. Thirteen contextual crops were initially created and inspected; a fourteenth, fondamental, isolated the adjective ending lying outside same_triangle. All fourteen saved crops were personally viewed. Every crop was made once at the listed original bounds, enlarged to width 3000 with LANCZOS, autocontrast and UnsharpMask(radius=1.05, percent=105, threshold=4). No OCR, outside research or compilation was used.

The sheet is upright main-hand working text. It carries 5 at the top and 119 at the lower right; both numbers are transcribed and inventoried, with no archive-marker-only comparison rows. There is no independent title or date. The original arrangement has the memory relations to the right of (17), then the large drawing on the left of the lower relation/prose, with its caption underneath. The proposed minipage/TikZ placement preserves that division without adding source prose.

An initial reader interpretation of a separate 2 before sommets was rejected after comparing the two displayed occurrences of the word on this page. Both begin with a detached angular 2-shaped s followed by the same low ommet run. Thus C’s les sommets is retained and H’s added numeral is rejected. This was a letterform comparison, not a mathematical argument about the number of endpoints.

Agreements personally retained in the opening paragraph include On a donc trouvé 4=1+3 présentations du groupoïde fondamental; the complete Pi_1 space/object-set expression; suivant qu’on utilise tous les chemins (8),(9), ou qu’on élimine les chemins a_r^i; et les sommets qui se trouvent dessus; Je vais maintenant examiner le cas où on élimine; deux côtés; i.e. où on ne garde les a_r^i que d’un seul type; disons les a_r^infinity; ce qui conduit aussi; tous les sommets proches des R_phi; de type; à ne garder que les R_r^{ij}; and the inserted pair condition. The un-hatted uppercase Pi, tilded X, S, every i/r/infinity index and the visible punctuation were read separately rather than supplied by context.

The revised paragraph has multiple independent source states: infini is struck and replaced by a small infinity; the leader for et ceux qui leur sont reliés attaches after that type; the cancelled centres clause continues onto faces at the next line; etc. is inserted above faces; les R_r^i is a separate cancellation; pour is on a short cancelled upper line; the later long index/verbal clause is independently crossed. The long cancelled phrase remains doubtful as a whole, especially where the strike merges with relation and word strokes. No unreadable part was filled merely to improve the grammar.

The fixed-index insertion has a closing parenthesis immediately after fixé and another after i=1; both remain. The phrase conduit aussi : éliminer keeps its colon and infinitive. The prose insertion (i,j) in {0,1} is retained as written; it is not silently changed to Cartesian-product membership to harmonize it with the explicit set-equality condition in (17).

In (17), the comma in R_r^{i,j}, the cursive script R and the two set braces were all read. In the memory formula, tau is a broad-topped curved stem, and the second right side is a closed Q with no raised 1,0. Q is retained even though the surrounding R family makes another R mathematically tempting. The first equality has a trailing comma. The outer enclosure has only three independent strokes, open at right; the curly brace inside it is separate.

All three rows of (18) were read, including every raised digit, lower r, arrow endpoint and cancellation. The first source’s possible comma is obscured by the adjacent hatching; 01 remains preferred with 0,1 as an alternative. The cancelled old arrow/letter remains unsure arrow-R. The cancelled Lambda’s prime and its preceding comma-like stroke are entangled with the hatching. The last two tau subscripts show small opening hooks and larger curved terminal strokes; parenthesized r is preferred, but C’s unparenthesized r plus final comma is retained as an alternative. These separator/parenthesis uncertainties do not change the mathematical indices.

In (19), both uppercase Lambdas are barless; the two prime-before-1 marks in the lower row are separate short uprights. The lower r, tau_1(r), tau_0(r), upper0/prime1, two equalities and two ones agree with the witnesses and are retained. The inserted avec and the words relations de redondance seulement were read, not inferred from the display. No mathematical proof is claimed by this visual check.

H’s separate drawing project files are not supplied, so only explicit statements in its supplied prose can be assessed. The general fan, arc-family and hatching description does not establish local directions, junctions, stroke counts or contour shapes. Those detailed geometric comparisons are therefore C-only when C differs; matching C geometry remains in the inventory and excluded-comparisons documentation, without an H error count. Distinct locally omitted labels and the small interior turn are recorded separately. No unavailable H drawing was inspected.

The drawing was traced locally against the C code: two pale rings, an uncircled lower-left infinity junction, the thin triangulating spokes, three pale diagonal interior strokes, three named path labels, seventeen typed vertex labels (one of them the unresolved outer 1), and the overworked central-right glyph are all present. Each of the ten small corner arcs has two separately retained heads. The doubled far-left loop and small interior turn remain distinct. The central-left tiny0 is added from the ink. An isolated dark speck above the central Lambda-prime label is not promoted to a new marked vertex or a character.

The southeast outer diagonal has one head toward the central junction; C’s detached short up-arrow is the same source head and is not duplicated. The inner southeast contour meets a dark lower closing segment above the lower-right circled infinity; its lower tip has no independently visible head. The rightmost sloping side has transverse/hooked hatches and no terminal head at its upper infinity, whereas the lower0-to-1 side has a clear rightward head. The nearby inward-sloping edge is retraced. The pale lower-left-infinity-to-lower1 connector omitted by C is restored. The overworked glyph above the central-right horizontal edge is graphical uncertainty, not an inferred vertex type.

The caption has an above-line faces insertion and no guillemets around arrondis. The closing prose retains ens. without expansion, the plain Pi_1(X), mais sur des ens. de sommets différents, savoir, and the S-S_i minus notation. The final tilde-X has two upper stars and a third lower one, plus a detached tiny horizontal tick beneath it; that tick is not declared a fourth star. The final closer after cas explicité favors ] but keeps ) as an alternative, with the round opening unchanged.

No independent mathematical proof, computation, certificate or use-and-recheck was performed on this leaf; check_events is empty. The assertion that only redundancy relations remain and the resulting free-groupoid presentation were transcribed, not independently established. Their correctness would depend on the earlier definitions and elimination argument, which were not reopened. There is no author-written explicit proof-check or doubt label identified on this leaf beyond its visible revisions/uncertain graphic ink.

Main identified one further textual duplication in H: faces appears both inside the earlier cancelled centres-clause transcription and again after the inserted word. The source has one cancelled faces with etc. above it. This is now a separate H-only row, supported by the existing revision_faces crop.
